title: How do we find ten marked angles?
description: Ten figures show parallel lines cut by a transversal, with one angle marked in each. Corresponding and alternate angles are equal, interior angles on the same side add up to one hundred and eighty degrees, and a final check ties the answers together.
teaching_notes: One idea: for each marked angle, pick the one relation between it and the given angle, either equal or adding up to one hundred and eighty degrees. Watch for angles in the figures that are shown but not needed.

video_script.why: The child applies the relations of the solved example to ten figures, choosing equal or adding up to one hundred and eighty each time.
video_script.substitution: the book's own ten figures, marked a to j, each with parallel lines and a transversal
video_script.anchor: ten small figures marked a to j, each with parallel lines, a transversal and one or two given angles
video_script.payoff_line: Every angle came from a parallel line rule or from a straight line

final_answer.spoken: eigh is forty eight degrees, b is fifty two degrees, c is eighty one degrees, d is ninety nine degrees, e is sixty nine degrees, f is forty eight degrees, g is one hundred and twenty two degrees, h is seventy five degrees, i is fifty four degrees, and j is ninety seven degrees

maths_rules: corresponding angles of parallel lines are equal, so a = 48
alternate angles of parallel lines are equal, so b = 52, e = 69, h = 75 and i = 54
interior angles on the same side add up to 180, so c = 180 - 99 = 81, d = 180 - 81 = 99 and f = 180 - 132 = 48
g matches the 122 degree angle at the other line, so g = 122
j is the vertically opposite angle of the corresponding angle of 97, so j = 97
angles shown but not needed are left out
video_script.design: Ten small figures in a row, each marked with its letter. The angle that is found takes the colour of the relation used: one colour for equal, another for adding up to one hundred and eighty.

narration: <bookmark mark='alt'/>Angles between parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal, are called alternate angles. They are equal.
<bookmark mark='int'/>Angles between parallel lines, on the same side of the transversal, are called interior angles.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Interior angles add up to one hundred and eighty degrees.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: a and 48° are corresponding angles, so a = 48°; b and 52° are alternate angles, so b = 52°

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step one, eigh and forty eight degrees are corresponding angles. They are equal, so eigh is forty eight degrees.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Then b and fifty two degrees are alternate angles. They are equal, so b is fifty two degrees.

marks.d: in figure d, 180 − 81 is written and d is marked 99°
marks.f: in figure f, 180 − 132 is written and f is marked 48°

beats.colours: the interior pairs share one colour
narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, c, d and f each have an interior angle on the same side. This is the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='c'/>The angle c is one hundred and eighty take away ninety nine, which is eighty one degrees.
<bookmark mark='d'/>The angle d is one hundred and eighty take away eighty one, which is ninety nine degrees.
<bookmark mark='f'/>The angle f is one hundred and eighty take away one hundred and thirty two. That is forty eight degrees.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: e, h and i are alternate angles of 69°, 75° and 54°, so e = 69°, h = 75°, i = 54°

<bookmark mark='h'/>The angle h and seventy five degrees are alternate angles, so h is seventy five degrees.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: g matches 122° at the other line, so g = 122°; j is the vertically opposite angle of the corresponding angle of 97°, so j = 97°

narration: <bookmark mark='g'/>Step four, g is in the matching corner at the other line.
<bookmark mark='geq'/>It matches one hundred and twenty two degrees, so g is one hundred and twenty two degrees.
<bookmark mark='j'/>The corresponding angle of ninety seven degrees is ninety seven degrees. Its vertically opposite angle is the same, so j is ninety seven degrees.
<bookmark mark='pair'/>Step five, to check, eighty one and ninety nine add up to one hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='line'/>One hundred and twenty two and fifty eight also add up to one hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Fifty four, seventy and fifty six lie on a straight line. They add up to one hundred and eighty.
